title: The Quran: Surah 67, al-Mulk (Sovereignty)
author: Tradução inglesa de Talal Itani (ClearQuran)
tradition: Texto sagrado do Islão, século VII
intro: Lição sobre a Surata 67. O texto inglês é a tradução de Talal Itani, reproduzida sem alterações; as notas de língua, perguntas, discussão e escrita são material pedagógico separado, baseado apenas no que o próprio texto diz. Cada nível estuda um excerto diferente.

source.title: Quran English Translation: Clear, Pure, Easy to Read Modern English
source.edition: Edition A (uses the word 'Allah' to refer to the Creator)

questions.q: According to verse 3, what does the speaker ask the reader to do?

options: thin breaks or faults in something

questions.q: Verse 3 says 'You see no discrepancy'. What is the speaker saying about the creation?
options: That the reader sees no fault or inconsistency in it
questions.why: 'No discrepancy' quer dizer que o leitor não vê incoerência nem falha.

questions.q: How many times does the word 'again' appear in verses 3 and 4?
questions.why: 'Look again' no versículo 3, e 'look again, and again' no versículo 4: três vezes.

questions.q: Which sentence best sums up verses 3 and 4?
options: The reader is told a story about a journey
The reader is given a list of rules
The reader is asked to count the layers
The reader is challenged to look for faults and ends with a dazzled and tired sight
questions.why: O versículo 3 desafia a procurar fendas e o versículo 4 diz que a vista volta 'dazzled and exhausted'.

B2.discussion: The passage challenges the reader to look again and again. Is it a good method to test an idea by looking at it repeatedly? Why?
B2.writing: Write 80 to 100 words: Say what the reader is asked to do and what happens in the end.

questions.q: According to verse 2, what did He create?
questions.why: O versículo 2 diz: 'He who created death and life'.

questions.q: Verse 2 says He created death and life 'to test you'. What does 'test' suggest about the purpose?
options: That the test is a game of chance
That the test has no purpose
questions.why: O texto diz 'as to which of you is better in conduct'.

questions.q: Verse 1 describes Him with two clauses. Which?
options: Who created death, and Who created life
Who is the Almighty, and Who is the Forgiving
In whose hand is the sovereignty, and Who has power over everything
questions.why: O versículo 1 tem 'in whose hand is the sovereignty' e 'Who has power over everything'.

options: The passage tells a story about a king
The passage lists laws about trade
The passage names who holds sovereignty and states the purpose of death and life
questions.why: O versículo 1 fala da soberania e o versículo 2 do propósito da morte e da vida.

C1.discussion: Verse 2 says death and life were created 'to test you'. How does presenting death and life together as one act change how the reader thinks about them?
C1.writing: Write 120 to 150 words: Explain how verse 2 builds on the claim of verse 1.

questions.why: O versículo 2 acaba com 'He is the Almighty, the Forgiving'.

questions.q: 'Dazzled and exhausted' (verse 4) describes the sight as:
options: overwhelmed and tired after looking so much

questions.q: What does the final result in verse 4 suggest about the search for cracks?
options: That the search is not made
That none is found, and the effort wears the viewer out
questions.why: O versículo 3 diz 'You see no discrepancy' e o versículo 4 diz que a vista volta deslumbrada e exausta.

questions.q: How does the passage shift between verse 2 and verse 3?
options: From statements about Him and what He created to direct address and a challenge to the reader
From a challenge to a story
From a list of places to a list of names
From a question to a rule
questions.why: O versículo 3 usa 'You see' e 'Look again'.

questions.q: Which description of the passage is best supported?
options: Two verses of statements about Him, then two verses that challenge the reader to look and look again
questions.why: Os versículos 1 e 2 são afirmações e os versículos 3 e 4 são o desafio ao leitor.

C2.discussion: The passage moves from statements to commands and a question addressed to the reader. What does this shift do to the reader's role?
C2.writing: Write 150 to 200 words: Analyse how the passage moves from statement to challenge, referring to specific words.
